title: Building a digital preparedness library
source: Original demonstration text created for Offline Field Library
text: A digital preparedness library stores reference material on a device before connectivity is lost. Start with a small selection of useful documents and test that you can open them without internet access. Organize content into packs such as equipment manuals, local plans, repair instructions and reference books. Keep the original title, publisher, revision date and license with every document. A source-backed assistant should retrieve relevant passages and show their document titles beside its answer. If the library has no relevant passage, use ordinary search or add a suitable document rather than inventing an answer. Keep another copy of important files on separate storage. Maps, course videos and language models each require their own storage budget. A phone can run the library itself; it does not need to act only as a client of a laptop.

title: Equipment manual record template
source: Original demonstration text created for Offline Field Library
text: For each piece of equipment, record its exact model name, serial number if appropriate, original manufacturer's manual, maintenance schedule and location. Keep setup instructions, compatible parts and your own maintenance notes with the manual. Verify that an instruction applies to the exact equipment model before following it. A general-purpose language model is not a substitute for the manufacturer's specification. In this prototype, field notes are stored separately from the document search index. Import a note as a document if you want it included in library retrieval.

title: Supply record and arithmetic example
source: Original demonstration text created for Offline Field Library
text: A supply record has an item name, quantity, unit, storage location and expiration date if relevant. Optional calories per unit should use the same unit as the recorded quantity. To calculate stored calories, multiply each item quantity by its entered calories per unit and sum the results. This arithmetic does not establish nutritional adequacy, food safety or a personal consumption requirement. Missing calorie entries count as zero in the prototype display. Editing quantities, consumption events, barcode lookup and water-duration calculations are future features; this preview supports adding records and exporting them.
